note: For spec/record-rules.md, "The card state file". `rules_version` is the version number of the rules the files with `record_rules_case` were computed by; when it goes up, they are computed again. `files`: card state files, valid or broken. `content` is the whole file as text; the file is the UTF-8 encoding of it (only broken files have a character outside ASCII). A file whose bytes are not UTF-8 has `content_hex` in place of `content`: its bytes as lowercase hex digits. `proof_log` says whose accepted scopes and platform table the file is read with (spec/scope.md). A valid file has `cards`: the rows as states, in the order of the file, each with the items of spec/record-rules.md, "State", and `last_seq`; `slots` has exactly the slots the row lists, so a platform that is not there is in the initial state, and null means none. Reading `content` gives `cards`; writing `cards`, given in any order and with or without slots in the initial state, gives `content`. A broken file has the number of the first line that fails (counting from 1) and the code. A valid file with `record_rules_case` is the final state of the case of that name in record-rules.json: its cards are that case's cards with `accounts` left out, the slots in the initial state left out, and `last_seq` the `seq` of the card's last valid result; `count` is the number of the case's events, the count the file would be published for. `rules_leave` false marks a file whose rows are well formed but are not states the rules leave. `comparisons`: a re-verifier's comparison ("Comparing"). `content` is a valid file, `count` the count of the fingerprint line of its date, `verified` the number of records the re-verifier has applied the rules to, `computed` its cards with a valid record among them, in the form of `cards`. `outcomes` has every card of the file or of `computed`, in the order of a file's rows, as `same`, `skipped` or `different`; `passes` is false if any is `different`. No implementation in this repository's TypeScript reads `comparisons`.

comparisons.name: every card the same
comparisons.note: The re-verifier has applied the rules to as many records as the file covers.

comparisons.name: no card and no row
comparisons.note: The empty file against a proof log without a valid record.

comparisons.name: the re-verifier is behind the file: rows beyond its records are skipped
comparisons.note: It has applied 2 records; the row with last_seq 3 is compared next time.

comparisons.name: the re-verifier is behind the file: a card that changed after its records is skipped, not compared with its older state
comparisons.note: The file has the card's state after record 3; the re-verifier has it after record 1.

comparisons.name: the re-verifier is ahead of the file: cards whose last valid record is after the count are skipped, with or without a row
comparisons.note: Records 4 and 5 were written after the file: a new card, and a withdrawal by a card of the file.

comparisons.name: a card with a valid record up to the count has no row
comparisons.note: Every card whose last valid record is at or before the count must have a row.

comparisons.name: a card with a valid record up to the count has no row, the re-verifier being ahead
comparisons.note: The card of record 4 is skipped; the card of record 2 is missing from the file.

comparisons.name: a row for a card the proof log gives no valid record
comparisons.note: The row's last_seq is within the records applied, and the re-verifier has no such card: record 2 was invalid, or is another card's.

comparisons.name: one item differs: switch_count
comparisons.note: Every item is compared.

comparisons.name: one item differs: current
comparisons.note: The file says the card withdrew; the proof log says it did not.

comparisons.name: one item differs: last_card_proof
only last_seq differs: the row is older than the card's last valid record, which is within the count
comparisons.note: The states are equal, but the file was to hold the state after record 3 and names record 1. Not skipped: the card did not change after the count.

comparisons.name: the row is older than the card's last valid record, which is within the count
comparisons.note: The file missed record 3. Not skipped: the card did not change after the count.

comparisons.name: the row names a later record than the card's last valid one, within the records applied
comparisons.note: The file says record 3 is a valid record of the card; the proof log says it is not.

comparisons.name: a slot the file lists and the proof log leaves in the initial state
comparisons.note: A platform without a slot, in the row or in the computed state, is the initial slot.

comparisons.name: a slot the proof log gives and the file leaves out
a row the rules cannot leave differs from every computed state
comparisons.note: The row is well formed; that it is not a state of the rules shows here.

comparisons.name: every last_seq far beyond the count: nothing is skipped, every card is different
comparisons.note: The server kept something else than a seq as last_seq. A row beyond the count is never the state after the first count records.

comparisons.name: every last_seq far beyond the count, the re-verifier far ahead of the count
comparisons.note: The same file with N far above the count: the outcome of a row beyond the count does not depend on N.

comparisons.name: a last_seq one beyond the count is different, the re-verifier at the count
comparisons.note: The largest last_seq a row can have is the count.

comparisons.name: a last_seq one beyond the count is different, the re-verifier behind the file
comparisons.note: Beyond the count comes before beyond N: the row is not skipped.

comparisons.name: a last_seq beyond the count is different even when it is the card's last valid record: the file was to stop at the count
comparisons.note: Record 4 is a valid record of the card and the row is its state after it; the file of count 3 was to hold its state after record 3.

comparisons.name: a row beyond the count for a card the proof log gives no valid record
comparisons.note: Count and N are 2; the row says record 3.

comparisons.name: a last_seq at the count, the re-verifier behind the file: skipped
comparisons.note: Rows with a last_seq above N and at most the count are compared the next time.

comparisons.name: a last_seq between N and the count for a card the re-verifier has in an older state: skipped
comparisons.note: The re-verifier has applied 1 record; the row is the card's state after record 2.

comparisons.name: one item differs: last_declared, of a slot that was withdrawn
comparisons.note: current is none on both sides. Whether the next account is a refresh or a switch depends on last_declared alone.

comparisons.name: one item differs: last_declared, current being set
comparisons.note: The row is not a state the rules leave (current is not last_declared); it is still compared item by item.
